entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zephyrinus, bishop of Rome from 199 to 217 CE, presided over the nascent Christian community in the heart of the Roman Empire during a period of intense theological fermentation and external pressure. His pontificate was crucial in shaping early Christian doctrine, particularly regarding the nature of Christ, amidst the rise of various Christological heresies. He succeeded Victor I and was, in turn, succeeded by his principal advisor, Callixtus I. His reign consolidated the authority of the Roman see in doctrinal matters during a critical era for the Church's self-definition.

Zephyrinus actively confronted emerging theological challenges, most notably Modalism (also known as Sabellianism), which posited that God manifested successively as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit rather than being co-existent persons of a Trinity. He excommunicated prominent Modalists such as Theodotus the Younger, a tanner from Byzantium, and his followers, known as the Theodotians, and later Noetus and Praxeas, staunchly upholding the distinct divinity of Christ against Unitarian interpretations. His administration also oversaw the development of the Coemeterium Callixti (Catacombs of Callixtus) along the Appian Way, though largely managed by Callixtus, providing a central burial ground for Roman Christians and a tangible symbol of their growing communal identity and organization.
